<reflection>
After three experiments, the fitting results show that M3 currently has the lowest cumulative negative log-likelihood, but the differences among M1–M19 are small (all within about 2.1 NLL units, except M20). This indicates that the data so far do not strongly discriminate among most candidate mechanisms. The experiments have varied catalyst concentration (0.01 and 0.05 M at fixed substrate) and added product (0.2 M at low catalyst), providing information on catalyst scaling and product effects. However, substrate concentration has remained constant at 1.0 M. To further reduce uncertainty, we need to probe the substrate dependence of the reaction, which is a key differentiator among mechanisms (e.g., Michaelis-Menten saturation, substrate inhibition, cooperative binding, or substrate-dependent deactivation). The aim of the third turn—testing product effects—was achieved, but more information is needed.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
I propose an experiment with lower substrate concentration (0.2 M) while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and no initial product. This design will reveal the reaction order with respect to substrate at a concentration well below the previous fixed value (1.0 M). Comparing the kinetic profile with run 1 (S=1.0, cat=0.01, P=0) will allow us to assess how the rate scales with substrate. Mechanisms differ in their substrate dependence: simple Michaelis-Menten (M1) predicts hyperbolic saturation; mechanisms with substrate inhibition (M7, M11, M16) may show rate suppression at high substrate; dimerization/cooperative mechanisms (M2, M3) could exhibit sigmoidal kinetics; and mechanisms with substrate-dependent deactivation (M11, M16) may show different relative decay rates at low vs high substrate. By choosing a moderate low substrate, we avoid extreme conditions that could collapse distinctions (e.g., very high substrate leading to universal saturation). This experiment is informative for many mechanisms simultaneously because substrate concentration is a fundamental variable in kinetic models.
</hypothesis>
